clue.text: Grass border parking?

parts.note: a hem is the folded border of a piece of cloth
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A query about whether the strip of lawn by the road is for parking cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp is the cannabis plant, and grass is slang for cannabis.

clue.text: Warning-Verne's captain is coming up!

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Captain Nemo commands the Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel

explanation.surface: An alarm cry that the famous submarine commander is surfacing.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign foretelling trouble, a portent or warning.

clue.text: Interior safari characters at a distance

indicators.note: the inside letters of the word safari give the run we want

explanation.surface: Remarks about wildlife seen far away from the inside of a safari vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar is an adverb meaning far off or from a long way away.

clue.text: There are no longer any passengers in this house

definitions.text: There are no longer any passengers in this house

parts.words: There are no longer any passengers in this house
parts.note: passengers here are passenger pigeons, extinct since 1914, so the building that housed birds now has none

explanation.surface: A building, perhaps a disused station, that sees no more travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovecot is a shelter for pigeons, and the passenger pigeon is now extinct.

clue.text: Wet policy laid down to protect the house

definitions.text: laid down to protect the house

parts.note: damp means slightly wet
a course of action is a policy

explanation.surface: A soggy plan established to safeguard a home, or perhaps a parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp-proof layer is built into a wall's base to stop moisture rising into a building.

clue.text: These groundsheets will never get warm!

definitions.text: These groundsheets will never get warm!

parts.words: These groundsheets will never get warm!
parts.note: groundsheets read as sheets of ground, layers of earth that stay frozen all year

explanation.surface: A camper complaining that their cold groundsheets never warm up.
explanation.definitionFit: Permafrost is soil that stays frozen through every season, in polar regions.

clue.text: One reads differences in watermarks

parts.note: watermarks taken as the levels the sea reaches, so the device records changes in water height

explanation.surface: Someone studying the faint marks pressed into paper to spot forgeries.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures the rise and fall of the sea's level at a harbour.

clue.text: Left blockhead idle

parts.note: an oaf is a stupid, clumsy person

explanation.surface: A dullard stays behind doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf is to lounge about doing nothing, a verb sense of idle.

clue.text: Fairly slow movement of house-god over poor quarter of city

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: a lar is a Roman household god
a ghetto is a deprived district of a city

explanation.surface: A household deity drifts slowly across a slum.
explanation.walkthrough: LAR, singular of the Lares, the Roman gods who guarded the home.
explanation.definitionFit: Larghetto is a musical direction for a piece played a little less slowly than largo.

clue.text: Overseas correspondent is writer on half-day closing

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: only half of the day's name is kept, its first three letters

parts.note: Friday is a day of the week
the end is the close of something

explanation.surface: A journalist abroad files copy when the office shuts early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-day' means half of FRIDAY, a day, leaving FRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen pal is someone, often abroad, with whom one exchanges letters.

clue.text: Fellow needs a hospital note

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A man needs a doctor's letter from the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: In tonic sol-fa, fah is the fourth degree of the scale.

clue.text: Bound, we hear, to be transported

indicators.note: signals that the word is spoken, and a different spelling entered

parts.note: wrapped means bound up in a covering

explanation.surface: Someone tied up and about to be carried off.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means carried away with delight, enraptured.

clue.text: Unit of work from the power-generator

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A measure of output from an electricity plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The erg is the CGS unit of energy or work, one ten-millionth of a joule.

clue.text: Sound effect used in opening of "Oedipus Rex"

definitions.text: Sound effect used in opening of "Oedipus Rex"

parts.words: Sound effect used in opening of "Oedipus Rex"
parts.note: the first two letters of the play's title, O and E, join into one gliding vowel sound

explanation.surface: Theatrical noise produced at the start of Sophocles' tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gliding vowel combining two sounds in one syllable, as the oe in Oedipus.

clue.text: One can pull a punch, for example

definitions.meaning: an animal used for hauling loads
a Suffolk Punch is a breed of heavy working horse

explanation.definitionFit: A heavy horse bred for hauling carts and ploughs; the Suffolk Punch is one breed.

clue.text: In favour of lightweight line-up?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a gramme is a very small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Backing a boxer in a lightweight bout.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme lists the order of items or acts, a line-up.

clue.text: Stark coat, perhaps, for serving soldiers?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the two words could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Asking whether a plain coat is suitable for troops on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are strips of toast for dipping into a boiled egg, a British breakfast habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack holds slices of toast upright at the breakfast table, where soldiers are served.

clue.text: This anchor needs Head Office approval

parts.note: OK means approval

explanation.surface: A news presenter needs sign-off from headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anchor' suggests a TV presenter, but it is the device that holds a boat fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A hook is a crook-shaped catch, and an anchor is a hooked device that grips the seabed.

clue.text: Spring exam connected with municipal office

parts.note: May is a spring month
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A spoken test held in springtime for a council post.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayoral relates to the mayor, head of a town council.

clue.text: True sea-change can be severe

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of the preceding words are altered in order

explanation.surface: A genuine transformation can be harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sea-change' looks like one phrase, but 'sea' is fodder and 'change' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means stern, strict or plain without ornament.

clue.text: Supporting opening of Brighton track events

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: racing is a sport held on tracks

explanation.surface: Backing the start of the race meeting at the seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is an English seaside resort; 'opening' suggests a launch event.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracing means giving support to, as a brace props a structure.

clue.text: Commotion makes one run on street

indicators.note: in an across clue, on puts the first pieces after the next

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A fuss is caused by someone jogging along the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a disturbance or flurry of excitement.

clue.text: Tree homes troubled this golfing group

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Golfers' wayward shots have damaged some treehouses.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a match of three players, one against two playing alternate shots.

clue.text: Mum's retired uncle in America

indicators.note: retired means going backwards, so in this down entry the letters are read upwards

parts.note: Ma's is another way of saying mum's

explanation.surface: Mother's brother has stopped working and lives in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Sam is the personification of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam stands for America and its government.

clue.text: Scottish port is always right

parts.note: ay (or aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A harbour town claims it is never wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a town and harbour on the Firth of Clyde in south-west Scotland.

clue.text: Japanese play, jolly average

parts.note: No (or Noh) is classical Japanese drama
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: A Japanese drama that is quite ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' here is the noun for a Royal Marine, not 'very'.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a standard or typical level, the average.

clue.text: Did he try this camel product as a universal solvent?

definitions.text: Did he try this camel product as a universal solvent?

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are worked into something new

explanation.surface: Wondering if someone made a camel extract to dissolve everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Alchemists sought the alkahest, a universal solvent; the whole clue is the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval practitioners of this early chemistry sought to turn base metals into gold.

clue.text: Like an evasive sort from English cathedral city

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Someone shifty from a Fenland town.
explanation.definitionFit: Eely means slippery and wriggling, hard to pin down.

clue.text: A bit charged on a Scottish island

parts.note: an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: A slightly expensive Hebridean holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, famous for its abbey.

clue.text: Cricket analysis?

definitions.meaning: an international cricket match between national sides
an examination or trial to find out what something contains

explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is international cricket, and a chemical test is an analysis.

clue.text: Gangway called for Man, for example

indicators.note: called means spoken, so the word is said rather than written

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between seats

explanation.surface: A passage was named after a man.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, an example of one.

clue.text: Benevolence of types holding marks

indicators.note: holding means one word contains the other

parts.note: kinds are types or sorts
lines are marks drawn on a surface

explanation.surface: Charitable nature shown by printing pieces bearing marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindliness is warmth and goodwill toward others.
